implemented_requirements.requirement: Three difficulty levels (beginner, intermediate, expert) with appropriate board sizes and mine counts
implemented_requirements.evidence: DIFFICULTIES = {"Beginner": (9, 9, 10), "Intermediate": (16, 16, 40), "Expert": (16, 30, 99)} in game.py and UI reads this dict to create new games.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can uncover cells by left‑clicking
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperUI.build_board creates a Button with command=lambda r=r, c=c: self.on_left_click(r, c); on_left_click calls self.game.reveal(r, c).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate adjacent mines
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperGame.place_mines computes self.board[r][c] = self.count_adjacent(r, c); UI refresh displays the number with btn.config(text=str(v) if v else "", ...).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Uncovering a mine ends the game with a loss
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperGame.reveal sets self.game_over = True and self.won = False when board[r][c] == -1; UI end_game shows "Boom! You hit a mine."

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board display updates after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperUI.refresh redraws every button based on game state after each click.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Flagging mechanism for suspected mines via right‑click
implemented_requirements.evidence: Button bind "<Button-3>" to on_right_click which calls self.game.toggle_flag(r, c); UI shows flag with text "F" and distinct colors.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Distinct visual representation for flagged cells
implemented_requirements.evidence: FLAG_BG = "#FFD700", FLAG_FG = "#CC0000"; UI config sets btn.config(text="F", bg=FLAG_BG, fg=FLAG_FG) for flagged cells.

judge.summary: The provided code implements a functional classic Minesweeper game with three difficulty levels, left‑click reveal, right‑click flagging, numeric hints, loss on mine, win detection, and a Tkinter GUI that updates the board and uses distinct visuals for flags. All core requirements are satisfied, and the code appears ready to run without missing pieces.
